question: Should exec denylist policy be persisted in both `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json`, or should one surface be the canonical owner?
rationale: The PR creates two unioned persisted policy sources at a privileged execution boundary; implementation review cannot choose the durable operator, editing, migration, and upgrade contract.

options.title: Single approvals-file owner
options.body: Keep denylist policy in `exec-approvals.json` and remove the parallel `tools.exec.denylist` surface, matching the repository's high bar for new config keys.

options.title: Dual unioned owners
options.body: Accept both persisted surfaces only with explicit precedence, editing, migration, and upgrade contracts across every execution host.

recommendation.title: Single approvals-file owner
recommendation.body: Keep denylist policy in `exec-approvals.json` and remove the parallel `tools.exec.denylist` surface, matching the repository's high bar for new config keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The current locked macOS delayed-authorization contract and recent adjacent merged work are directly tied to this owner.
